answer: Charge each identity a decaying deposit that is refunded only in small tranches per audited epoch. New agents enter through a narrow inlet where every claim needs two independent signatures, and the signal channel flags any account whose task variance looks cloned. A nadir check triggers when an agent's success rate drops below the peer median, forcing a full re-verification before further withdrawals. Duplicating identities now requires real deposits, honest variance and fresh attestations, so farms bleed capital faster than they can mint accounts.
